page.layout: One page of text, one column of running text; below it a note-line block on the left (catchwords and date of the dedication) with a centred signature line; a catchword at the lower right; a note at the lower right margin area. Notes in the right margin: none beside the text except a marginal note line set beside the dedication date.

main_text.l: sint, & ego eorum hæres, adeoque persolvere
damnas, ἀντάξιον affectui, quo familiam nostram
amplecteris, persolvere non queam; hunc re-
pendo legum codicem. Quem in se si spectes,
observabis exiguitatem; sin animum meum
unde promanat, affectus debiti amplitudinem.
Quæ licet nihil tuo fastigio satis dignum edere
queat; perpetuum tamen in te tuosque obser-
vantiæ pignus prodere gestit. Vtinam, vir nobi-
lissime, tantum placere & probari possit labor
meus, quantum ipse cum meis omnibus N.&A.
vestræ placere & probari annitor. Votis etiam
apud Deum contendens, ut Pater illi Iesu Chri-
sti, Spiritum suum cum omnibus quæ expe-
diunt bonis, in dies magis magisque effundat, vi-
tamque in Reipublicæ & in ea Ecclesiæ incolu-
mitatem, quam diutissime proroget
Dabam Lugd.Bat. ipsis Id. Aug. anno partæ salutis 1637.
Nobilitati & Amplitudini vestræ:
cujus cliens permanere gaudeo
C. L'EMPEREVR ab OLWYCK.

page.notes: The text is partly faded; the catchword and the lower-right lines are partly obscured. Greek word "ἀντάξιον" is a best reading of the printed Greek on the line "damnas, ἀνταξίοι". The printed marginal note "Nobilitati & Amplitudini" stands in the line beside "Dabam".
